text: Photons do not interact, so a deterministic two-qubit gate seems impossible in linear optics. What did Knill, Laflamme and Milburn (2001) use to escape this?
choices: A strong optical (Kerr) nonlinearity acting directly between the photons
Cooling the photons until they begin to interact
Slowing light in a resonator so the photons collide
Measurement (photodetection of ancilla photons), which is not a linear operation and supplies the missing nonlinearity
explanation: KLM's insight is that photodetection is nonlinear: interfering data photons with ancillas and post-selecting on a heralding detector pattern applies a transformation no linear circuit can. No inter-photon interaction, Kerr medium, cooling, or collision is used (choices 0-2); the nonlinearity comes entirely from measurement.
